extraction_notes: Forward, reverse, junction-capacitance, and power-derating curves were digitized directly from the supplied vector plots on p. 2; no intermediate curve points were synthesized.

Fig. 1 contains two typical traces labelled TA=25 degC and TA=100 degC in the grouped B5817W THRU B5819W datasheet; the figure does not assign a part-specific trace. Forward-current values use the plotted A axis.
Fig. 2 contains TA=25 degC and TA=100 degC typical reverse-current traces. Reverse current is represented as positive magnitude and normalized from the plotted mA axis to A in the curve points.

Fig. 3 is a typical junction-capacitance curve at TA=25 degC and f=1 MHz with logarithmic axes; capacitance values are normalized from the plotted pF axis to F. The table separately specifies typical CJ=120 pF at VR=4.0 V and f=1 MHz.
Fig. 4 power derating has direct plotted vertices at PD=500 mW from TA=0 to 25 degC and at PD=0 mW at TA=150 degC; values are normalized to W.

Absolute-rating bounds for B5817W at TA=25 degC are VRRM=20 V, VRMS=14 V, VDC=20 V, IF(AV)=1.0 A, and IFSM=9.0 A at t=8.3 ms half-sine wave. The datasheet also lists PD=500 mW, Tj=-55 to +150 degC, Tstg=-55 to +150 degC, and RthetaJA=250 degC/W on p. 1.

The datasheet publishes no reverse-recovery-time, breakdown-voltage, or breakdown-current specification; VRRM and VDC ratings are limits, not breakdown data. The separate IR2 maximum is 10 mA at VR=VDC and TA=100 degC and is not used as the room-temperature reverse-current fit target.
